content.content:
# JusPrin's translations JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for (`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a translation file: | Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL` | `native/.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n//.mo`, the catalog the app loads | | The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) | Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of `native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used. ## Updating the catalogs After marking or changing text: ```bash python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py ``` It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new entry in every `.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's `AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: ` where the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder. The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like `<0>…` for elements inside a `Trans`, and `{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`). ## Marking text Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items, tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly as it was. Leave these in English, unmarked: - **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown. - Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes, test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code. - Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`, `report_error`): they are read by developers. - Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names. ### In the pages ```tsx import { t, plural } from '@lingui/core/macro'; import { Trans } from '@lingui/react/macro';

Takes effect when {app} restarts. Your project is saved first.

const label = plural(count, { one: '# printer', other: '# printers' }); const title = t({ message: 'Back', context: 'navigation' }); // a word with several meanings const hint = t({ message: 'Fit', comment: 'Verb: scale the model to the plate' }); // a note for translators ``` - One message per sentence. Never build a sentence from translated pieces, and never splice a translated word into another sentence: use a placeholder, or a `Trans` with the element inside it. - A count needs `plural` / `Plural`, not "printer(s)". - Put only plain variables in placeholders (`{name}`, not `{a.b.c}`): the translator sees the variable's name. Pull an expression into a well-named local first. - The language is chosen before the first render and never changes while a page runs, so `t` works anywhere, including at a module's top level and in plain `.ts` files. `Trans` and `useLingui` from the macros need no provider (see `i18n.tsx`). - Tests run in English, so a test that finds text by its English words keeps working. ### In the native code - `_L("…")` gives a `wxString` for a window; `_u8L("…")` gives UTF-8 for JSON sent to a page. - Translate when the text is used, never in a static initializer, which runs before the language is loaded. Mark such a table with `L("…")` and call `_L`/`_u8L` on the entry where it is shown. - Use `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)` rather than concatenation, and `_L_PLURAL` for counts; `// TRN` above a string tells the translator what it means. - Every file that marks text is extracted: `update_catalogs.py` reads every `.cpp` and `.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` except `Testing/`. Do not add JusPrin files to `localization/i18n/list.txt`. # Translation rules The rules a translation must follow, condensed from the wiki's [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md), the [glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) and the localization section of `AGENTS.md`. `po_tool.py apply` rejects the mechanical violations it can detect; everything else is on the translator. ## Mechanical: enforced by `apply` A rejected entry is not written. Fix it and apply again. - **Placeholders stay exactly as written:** `%s`, `%d`, `%.1f`, `%1$d`, `%1%`, `%%`. Never `%1 %`, never `%` for `%%`. Plain printf placeholders keep their order; only positional ones (`%1$s`, `%1%`) may move, and one the msgid repeats may appear just once. A broken placeholder crashes the app. - **Line breaks:** the same number of `\n`, with the same leading and trailing ones. Don't add breaks to fit text, least of all in parameter names. - **Leading and trailing spaces** are kept. A leading space usually means the string is appended to another. - **HTML tags** are kept, and the text between them is translated: `Click here to install it.` - **`℃`** (U+2103) stays one character, written exactly as in the source: `%d℃`, never `°C`, `° C` or `%d ℃`. - **Tokens stay verbatim:** `{placeholders}`, `[macros]`, G-code commands (`M141`, `G28`). Setting keys in snake_case (`use_relative_e_distances`) are flagged as warnings, because a few snake_case msgids are really labels (`top_front`). Keep a key unless the string uses it as a display name. - **Plural entries** need every form from the catalog's `Plural-Forms` header (`nplurals`: 1 for ja/ko/zh/th/vi, 3 for ru/cs/pl/lt, 4 for uk). Each form is really inflected for its quantity. Repeating one sentence is a bug in Slavic and Baltic languages, but correct in Turkish and Hungarian. ## A person's translation: patch it, don't rewrite it A translator's wording is kept unless it is wrong. Machine output never replaces it wholesale. - **A reworded string:** `pending` lists earlier translations of similar English under `similar`, and marks a person's work with `"human": true`. When the English barely changed, start from that translation and change only what the English change requires: a renamed term, an added clause, a period. Keep the translator's wording, word order, terms and line structure. If they already wrote what the new English says, the translation does not change at all. - **A fix in a person's translation:** for a check error (a line break, a space, placeholder order, a missing clause), change only what the error needs. Keep the rest of their words, even where they differ from the glossary or from how you would phrase it. Report such glossary differences instead. - **Rewrite only what is plainly wrong:** another string's text, a cut-off sentence, a mistranslation. Say why with `"rewrite": ""` in the item; the reason becomes the review note. - `apply` enforces this. It rejects text that strays further from a person's translation than the English change explains (below 85% alike for a fix, or clearly less alike than the English for a reworded string), unless the item carries `rewrite`. - Apply a fix that keeps the person's words with `--human`, so the entry stays theirs. Text you wrote gets the default `# AI Translated`. ## Mechanical: not detectable, still required - Edit only `msgstr`. Never change `msgid`, `msgctxt`, the header or another entry's text. - **Ending punctuation follows the source:** no added period, and no dropped one. `apply` warns. - Units follow the SI convention of the language: `s`, not `sec`. A parameter description holds no unit, because the field shows it. - **A button or short label holds one translation:** no alternatives in parentheses. They widen the control. - Don't use `fuzzy` for uncertainty. Fuzzy entries are hidden, and users then see English. ## Context: know what the string is before choosing its words English reuses one word for different things, and a string seen alone often reads several ways. Settle what each entry is before translating it. `pending` gives every entry the context the source holds: `refs` (where it is used), `code` (the lines around the use, for short strings and placeholder strings) and `nearby` (the translated short strings used next to it). `lookup --code` shows the same for existing entries. The catalogs themselves carry no source references. - **What kind of text it is,** from `code`: a button or menu item is a command, a field label or column header names a value, a checkbox states something that is on or off, and a tooltip, status line, error or dialog title each have their own register. Keep a label as short as a label. - **What it belongs to.** A setting's strings sit together in `PrintConfig.cpp`: `this->add("", …)`, then `label`, `category`, `tooltip`, `sidetext`. The tooltip describes that option, and quotes the label exactly as `nearby` shows it translated. The items of one menu, choice or toolbar (`enum_labels`, `Append`, an array of names) are a set: give them one grammatical form, and words that tell them apart. - **`msgctxt` separates homonyms.** `Back` in *Camera View* is the rear view, and `Back` in *Navigation* is the go-back button. Translate each context on its own. - **Overloaded English: translate the meaning.** - *Flow ratio* is a multiplier, *Flow Rate* is throughput, and *Flow Dynamics* is pressure compensation. These are three different terms. - *Extruder* can mean the toolhead, the feeder motor ("High extruder current on filament swap") or the nozzle ("all extruders must have the same diameter"). - *Home* is the homing move ("Please home all axes"), the home page, or the Home key (*Keyboard Shortcut*), which takes the name printed on that language's keyboards. *Fill* is infill, gap fill, or the paint tools' bucket and smart fill. *Normal* is the ordinary kind ("Normal support", "Normal printing") or the surface normal ("Normal X", "Smooth normals"). *Model* is the 3D model, or the printer model in "Model:". *Process* is the process preset, or an operation under way ("the slicing process"). - The glossary's rows record the senses that recur (`Plate` versus `Bed / Build plate`, `Feature (print)` versus `Feature (Design)`); the code tells which one a string means. - **Check the meaning in the code** when the English leaves it open: read the call site, and further in the file when `code` is not enough. - See what each placeholder is filled with. A fallback string substituted into a sentence must fit the slot it fills. - Settle the semantics the English blurs: a ratio or a difference, which way a rotation turns, which control a hint names. - **A msgid used in several places** (`left` is a view name and a hotend; `Sphere` is a primitive and a paint brush) needs a wording that fits every use. When none can, report the missing `msgctxt` as a source problem. - **When the context still leaves two readings,** take the likelier one and add a review note naming the other. ## Choosing the words - **The glossary is binding.** Use the language's rendering for every glossary term the `pending` output lists, inflected as the sentence needs. - **Rows that share a base term are different senses:** `Seam` (the print seam) versus `Seam (UV)` (the unwrap cut), and `Instance` versus `Instance (application)`. Pick by the description. - **A qualified row may be a false match.** `Feature (Design)` does not apply to "features of the app". - **A cell marked ⚠ (or holding two renderings) is unsettled.** Use the form the catalog already uses for that sense (`lookup`), and flag the entry for review. - **Kept in English:** brand and product names (OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, Orca Cloud, AMS, Micro-Lidar), acronyms (FDM, LAN, HTTPS), file formats, material codes (PLA, PETG-CF), G-code, macros and variables stay as written. In "Adaptive Pressure Advance", only "Pressure Advance" stays English. See the glossary page's *Kept in English* table. - **Language specifics** on the glossary page (`po_tool.py glossary --lang L` prints them) override general habits for that language. - **The catalog's existing words come next.** A tooltip or message that names a setting, a button or a menu item quotes that control's translation exactly, so the text matches what the user sees. `nearby` shows the controls next to the string; `lookup` finds the rest. For a recurring term the glossary lacks, `lookup` the English and `lookup --msgstr` the rendering you intend, and use the one the catalog already settled on in that sense. Reuse obsolete (`#~`) entries as a translation memory. - **No settled term: look outside the catalog, in this order.** 1. **Other slicers' shipped catalogs** for the same language: [BambuStudio](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio) `bbl/i18n//BambuStudio_.po` and [PrusaSlicer](https://github.com/prusa3d/PrusaSlicer) `resources/localization//PrusaSlicer_.po` (a local clone, if there is one). Orca shares much of its UI with both, so their translators have often rendered the same string already. Their choice is evidence, not a rule: the glossary and Orca's own catalog win. 2. **The 3D-printing community in that language:** manuals, wikis and forums of printer vendors (Bambu Lab, Prusa, Creality, Snapmaker) and their users. Take the term printers actually use, a loanword where they use the loanword. 3. **Neighbouring fields,** when printing has no term of its own: CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion, Onshape, AutoCAD), CNC/CAM and machining, then engineering and mathematics. General UI vocabulary (*Settings*, *Preferences*, *Undo*, *Browse*, *Quit*, *Copy*, *Paste*) follows the operating systems' own translations, which users already know. 4. **English,** when nothing is established: brand names, acronyms, file formats, G-code tokens, variables, and Orca-specific feature names with no equivalent. Translate paired terms as a pair, so they read as the two sides of one choice (direct drive and Bowden, inner and outer wall). Name the sources a term came from in the report. - **Each field keeps its own vocabulary.** 3D-view and CAD strings follow CAD software and drafting standards: the standard view names, *isometric*, *orbit*, *pan* and *zoom*, *cut plane* versus *section plane*, the primitive names. The camera of the 3D view (the viewpoint) and the printer's camera (the device) are different things and take different words wherever the language has two. - **A regional variant is its own language.** Never derive one from the other character by character or word by word: zh_TW and zh_CN differ in vocabulary, not only in script. Start from the variant's own glossary column and catalog. A converter (OpenCC `s2twp` for zh_CN → zh_TW) gives a draft at most; review every entry it produced. - **Boilerplate stays uniform.** `Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?` and `If expressed as a %, it will be computed over …` each get one template in the language, even where the English varies. ## Style - **Localize, don't translate word-for-word.** Translate what the string means where it appears (see *Context*), not each English word. - **Write native UI text.** The result should read as if the app had been written in that language. - Restructure the sentence instead of following English word order. - Break up long noun chains. - Drop passive and filler constructions the language doesn't use in UI text. - Don't calque English idioms or compounds where the language has its own expression. - Don't carry English Title Case over: capitalize as the language does (sentence case in most, German nouns as German writes them). - Use the language's own punctuation. Don't carry English marks over, such as ` — ` or straight quotes where the language has its own. ASCII quotes around a literal value the user types or the app matches stay as written. - **Follow the catalog's conventions,** which a new entry must match: - formal or informal address; - full-width or half-width punctuation; - spacing between scripts (CJK next to Latin letters or digits); - the separator sibling labels use before their value; - the verb form of buttons and menu commands (infinitive, imperative or noun); - the form of a confirmation question. - **Simplify developer phrasing** when the meaning survives. *"This option determines whether OrcaSlicer should apply the retract reduction on infill"* reads better as *"Disable retractions while printing infill."* Introduce nuances in following sentences, not in one packed clause. - **Don't expand.** A machine translation adds no facts the English doesn't state. Expanding descriptions is for human translators, who can confirm the extra content. - **Write for both audiences:** professionals and people with a printer at home. Keep the established terminology, used as plainly as the string allows. - **Read the batch back without the English** before applying it, as a user of the app would see it. Rewrite whatever reads like a translation, is ambiguous on its own, or uses a word differently from the strings around it. ## When to add a review note Add `"review": ""` to an item when the translation is probable but unconfirmed. It becomes `# Needs human review: …`, and the entry still ships. Typical reasons: - The English stays ambiguous even with its code: "Tile" as a verb or a noun. - A short label's role shows only in the running app, not in its code. - Two established terms compete, or the glossary cell is unsettled. - The string's grammar depends on a value substituted at runtime: `%zu %s` counts with no plural entry. Say exactly what to look at and where: *"Row name in the Design tab tool-offer menu; check it reads right for the whole row."* ## Problems that belong in the source, not the translation Report these; don't work around them in a catalog. - **The English is wrong.** Never "fix" it in the translation only. - **A hint names a control that doesn't exist,** or a user-visible literal isn't wrapped in `_L`. - **One msgid needs two translations.** The source needs `_L_CONTEXT` / `_u8L_CONTEXT` (a code change). - **A literal `%` in a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format`** fails `msgfmt`. Wipe	Wiping the nozzle tip clean / relieving nozzle pressure. Distinct from Flush / Purge, which clears the previous material out of the nozzle channel.	เช็ดหัวฉีด
Support interface	The denser layers between the support and the model surface it touches. Not the prime-tower Interface layer.	ผิวสัมผัสส่วนรองรับ
Model	A whole 3D object on the plate. Where a string covers both a model and its parts, prefer the neutral "object".	โมเดล
Part	A component of a model. Where a string covers both a model and its parts, prefer the neutral "object".	ชิ้นส่วน
Volume	A solid body making up a model; a negative volume is a cut-out. Not the numeric volume measurement.	ปริมาณ
Texture	The image painted onto a surface (custom plate image, model UV map) - not the *textured* rough finish of a plate, fuzzy skin or top surface, which is a different word in most languages.	พื้นผิว
Gizmo	An on-canvas manipulation tool (move/scale/rotate handles, cut, paint...).	กิสโม่
Adaptive bed mesh	Bed levelling that probes only the area the print occupies, instead of the whole bed.	ตาข่ายฐานพิมพ์ปรับได้
Damping	The damping ratio used by input shaping when computing damped oscillations.	การทำให้หมาด ๆ
Snake	Object-instance print order that walks the plate in a serpentine, row-by-row path (refined with 2-opt). The movement pattern — not the animal, and distinct from the Zig Zag infill pattern.	แบบงูเลื้อย
Nearest-neighbor	The default object-instance ordering heuristic: each next instance is the closest one not yet visited (“nearest-neighbor chaining”, then refined with 2-opt). It has no standalone msgid — it appears inside the print-order tooltip. Not the “Nearest” seam position, which is a different setting.	เพื่อนบ้านที่ใกล้ที่สุด
Design (tab)	The main tab for parametric CAD modelling, next to Prepare and Preview; "New Design" starts a new model there.	ออกแบบ
Sketch	A 2D drawing (lines, arcs, circles, splines) made on a plane or a face in the Design tab, which features such as Extrude or Revolve turn into a solid.	สเก็ตช์
Constraint	A geometric or dimensional rule between sketch entities (horizontal, parallel, tangent, coincident, a fixed distance…) that the sketch solver keeps satisfied.	เงื่อนไขบังคับ
Dimension (sketch)	A driving measurement (length, distance, radius, angle) placed on sketch geometry; editing its value resizes the sketch. Not the object's size ("Dimensions").	มิติ
Construction geometry	Sketch lines and arcs used only as references for drawing and constraints; they are not part of the profile. Toggled with "Construction".	เรขาคณิตช่วยสร้าง
Extrude	Design-tab feature that pushes a closed sketch profile, or a picked face, along a straight direction to add or remove material. Not the G-code viewer's Extrude move type.	ยืดขึ้นรูป
Revolve	Design-tab feature that spins a sketch profile around an axis to make a solid of revolution.	หมุนขึ้นรูป

content.text:
Both Thai catalogs are fully translated, and both required checks pass.

**Checks**
- `msgfmt --check-format --check-header` on `native/th.po` exits 0. It only warns that three header fields (`PO-Revision-Date`, `Last-Translator`, `Language-Team`) still hold their template defaults; I didn't touch the header.
- `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts -t '^th catalogs'` passes both tests (native and page).

**Entries translated**
- Native file: all 513 entries, each marked `# AI Translated`. The header allows Thai only one plural form, so the 17 plural entries now keep `msgstr[0]` only, the same way `ja.po` does.
- Page file: all 898 entries, each marked `# AI Translated`. Thai plural messages use only the `other` branch, and the `=1` branches from the source are kept.
- I made no other changes: no msgid, comment or entry order was altered, and nothing is committed.

**Flagged `# Needs human review`: 37 entries (13 native, 24 page).** The main reasons:
- **The same English needs two Thai words.** "Plate" means the build-plate type in the add-printer form (ฐานพิมพ์) but a project plate in All settings (เพลต). "Search models" is used for both AI models (โมเดล) and printer models (รุ่น). These may need a `msgctxt` added in the source.
- **The source doesn't say what a word refers to.** Examples are "it"/"them" in All settings, "Move to front", and what "%d on a marked face" is counting.
- **Product names.** I translated "Bring Your Own AI" (ใช้ AI ของคุณเอง) and the model tiers Standard/Expert (มาตรฐาน/ผู้เชี่ยวชาญ). The product may want the English names kept.
- **Formatting.** Thai date order puts the day first (`%2% %1%`), and whether to show the Gregorian or Buddhist-era year is open. Where the English joins two sentences with a period, I used a middle dot.
- **A few technical strings,** such as "bridge handshake" and "Not listening yet".

**Terminology a reviewer should know**
- **AI:** kept as "AI".
- **Chat:** แชท. A conversation is บทสนทนา.
- **Preset:** พรีเซ็ต, from the glossary and upstream's catalog.
- **Plate:** เพลต for a project plate, from the glossary. The physical bed or build-plate type is ฐานพิมพ์ or แผ่นฐานพิมพ์.
